extracted.intended_audience: judges, court administrators, policymakers, IP practitioners, and patent attorneys (particularly those involved with the Patent Court of Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and recommendations on institutional design, procedures, staffing, and internationalization measures for a national specialized Patent Court (Korea). Focuses on improving expertise, procedures, jurisdiction, infrastructure, and international outreach to raise trial quality and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive jurisdiction for IP administrative revocation and civil appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Court has exclusive jurisdiction over suits against decisions of KIPO/IPTAB and, since January 1, 2016, jurisdiction over appeals against district court decisions in civil actions relating to IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusive jurisdiction is presented as central to making the Patent Court a truly specialized forum responsible for sophisticated factual and legal disputes in science and technology and for resolving inconsistency and delays arising from prior two-track jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and operation of an International Division (foreign-language proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments permit proceedings in a foreign language and establishment of a dedicated International Division that allows oral arguments in a foreign language (effective June 13, 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare practice directions, secure professional interpreters, publish bilingual IP law resources (Korea-English/English-Korea IP law dictionary), and translate decisions to support international cases and use Patent Court decisions as international references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthening judicial expertise via targeted staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Place judges with science/engineering backgrounds, judges dedicated to handling IP matters, and lawyers/patent attorneys with long patent-practice experience; secure and retain highly skilled professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate trainees from Judicial Research & Training Institute with science/engineering, recruit judges specialized in IP, and take measures to retain them long-term to ensure competence in technical fact-finding and legal adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployment and empowered role of judicial technical examiners and research officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy judicial technical examiners (from KIPO and court-hired) and judicial research officers to participate in hearings and trials; examiners may seek clarification from parties on technical matters and state opinions for judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase number and disciplinary spread of examiners (machinery, chemistry, medicine, electronics, telecom, etc.), have them conduct prior investigation and review of relevant science/technology, and support judges in ensuring parties understand technical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of electronic litigation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide electronic litigation service to promote convenience and enable the court to proceed more quickly and efficiently (introduced 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High uptake (96.9% of 977 cases proceeded using electronic filing as of 2016) demonstrates efficiency gains; courts should continue to expand electronic filing to improve processing speed and party convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of procedural guidelines to increase predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Enact and publish Guidelines of Civil Practice and Procedure and Guidelines of Revocation of Administrative Decision to provide predictability of trial procedure and enable better preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines lay foundation for active case management and intensive issue-by-issue hearings; they should be improved for efficiency and reasonableness and updated as needed to match procedural needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiated case management and issue-by-issue hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use differentiated case management by disputed issues, dedicated oral and intensive hearings, and issue-by-issue hearings to achieve fair and expeditious trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active case management tailored to dispute complexity helps allocate resources, shorten handling periods, and promote thoroughness in technical fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil mediation tailored to IP disputes (Internal Regulation on Patent Court Mediators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a civil mediation division with mediators composed of legal and technical experts; forward cases to mediation prior to the first trial date to minimize costs and promote early resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt 'Delegated Mediation System' to allow mediators to conduct sessions in other courts' facilities (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Smart Work Center); enter MOUs with specialized IP ADR organizations (IIPAC) to coordinate external mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of a special division for precedent-significant cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a special division to handle cases of significant social importance or cases that may yield decisions distinct from traditional legal principles or practices (established March 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use special division for high-impact matters (example: pharmaceutical patent term extension cases) to ensure concentrated expertise and coherent precedent formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthening hearing quality and maturity of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure hearings are fair, thorough, and that decisions are sophisticated and match global standards; improve procedural guidelines and substantive decision quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial technical examiners and research officers should perform prior technical review; judges should ensure parties understand relevant science/technology and employ technical advisors, expert witnesses, and appraisals to support careful adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationalization and development of an IP Hub Court (outreach & research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the Patent Court as a preferred global IP litigation forum and an Asian patent dispute resolution organization by hosting international conferences, dispatching judges internationally, and building networks of national and international experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish International IP Law Research Center, secure full-time researchers, publish annual English IP Law Journal and English Patent Court Decisions, and translate decisions to enhance international influence and cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance competence, professionalism, and fairness of judges for international credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority and reliability of decisions in international cases depend on judges' competence, professionalism, and fairness; therefore, measures must promote internationalization and specialization of judges and judicial technical examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in judge training, international exchanges, language capability, and specialist recruitment so foreign parties and courts regard decisions as authoritative and reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand exclusive jurisdiction to cover civil infringement motions and criminal cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue legislative changes so the court's exclusive jurisdiction includes appeals from motions such as preliminary injunctions and, in the long term, first-instance trials and appeals in criminal cases related to patent and other IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including such matters under exclusive jurisdiction aims to enable prompt and consistent adjudication of main claims and motions, reduce inconsistency and delay arising from jurisdictional separation, and improve IP protection at an early stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and institutional infrastructure to support IP specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish physical facilities (small courtrooms per division, dedicated court building) and institutional arrangements (increased court divisions, staffing) to process increasing and complex IP caseloads efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocate near research clusters (e.g., Daejeon/Daedeok Science Town, KAIST) to benefit from proximity to technical expertise; build facilities anticipating future expansion in panels and judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical monitoring for case filing, handling, and cross-border trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and analyze statistics on number and types of cases filed, handling/results (decisions, withdrawals), revocation rates, handling periods, and cross-border case composition to inform resource allocation and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: tracking that 93.1% of revocation cases were handled within one year (1998–2017), revocation rates per case type (patent 26.9% vs. utility model 33.4%), and foreign-party proportions (~30%) supports planning for staffing, expertise, and internationalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: External advisory bodies and expert facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Judicial Administration Advisory Committee and Scientific Advisory Committee to seek objective and specialized advice from external experts; facilitate expert witnesses, technical advisors, and appraisals; permit inventors to make statements upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external committees and experts to supplement internal expertise, lend objectivity, and assist in complex technical determinations.
